    Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis

    Source: R/meta-sensitivity.R
    meta_leave1out.Rd

    meta_leave1out() refits the meta-analysis k times, each time leaving out one study, to show how much the pooled estimate and the heterogeneity depend on any single study.

    Usage

    meta_leave1out(
  .data,
  yi = .yi,
  vi = .vi,
  method = "REML",
  test = "z",
  level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A <meta_fit> from meta_pool() (its estimator and test are reused), a <meta_es> or a data frame.

    yi, vi

    <data-masking> Columns holding the effect sizes and sampling variances. Default to .yi and .vi.

    method, test

    Used only when .data is not a <meta_fit>.

    level

    Confidence level for intervals.

    Value

    A tibble with one row per omitted study: study, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, conf.low, conf.high, tau2, I2, H2, QE and p.QE.

    References

    Viechtbauer, W. and Cheung, M. W.-L. (2010). Outlier and influence diagnostics for meta-analysis. Research Synthesis Methods, 1(2), 112-125. doi:10.1002/jrsm.11

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg,
  study = author
)
meta_pool(bcg) |> meta_leave1out()
